label: lifecycle

rule.gopls: the first release (vX.Y.0) of every minor line v0.16 ... v0.23 (the campaign's v0.23.0), plus the newest
rule.rust-analyzer: the first weekly release (tag YYYY-MM-DD) of each quarter 2024-Q4 ... 2026-Q3, plus the campaign's 2026-09-21 and the newest
rule.ts6: the last patch of each TypeScript minor 5.5, 5.6, 5.7, 5.8, 5.9 and 6.0, each with the typescript-language-server release newest at that TypeScript release's publication time (npm `time`), plus the campaign pair 6.0.3+tsls6.0.0 and the newest pair
rule.ts7: every TypeScript 7.x version on npm up to the newest stable one (stable and beta/rc releases; nightly -dev builds excluded)

common: releases published up to 2026-09-28; 3 replays per group and build; verdicts of version_sweep.verdict

ts6 line through the frozen sweep's kind tsserver (pinned wrapper started with the pinned tsserver.js, no ts6 session settings), as older-2025 and ts_isolation.py; the campaign pair in that kind controls for the kind

gopls builds are compiled and run with the local Go (go1.27.1, the toolchain of the campaign's v0.23.0 build); a release the local Go cannot compile is compiled and run with go1.24.4 (install_builds --go); where the install directory already holds an era-Go benchmark build, the local-Go build goes to gopls-<v>+<go>/

a gopls group is replayed on a build only if the build's Go meets every go directive of the group's project (go.mod/go.work), since the harness runs gopls with GOTOOLCHAIN=local; other pairs are listed under skip
a build that cannot be installed or launched after two attempts is recorded as unavailable
the C2 group (timing race) runs alone; otherwise at most 3 jobs at once (gopls, rust-analyzer, ts6+ts7)
